gaps.sentence: The audience always ___ when the curtain falls.
gaps.explanation: 'Always' marks a general habit, which takes the present simple: claps.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry, I ___ you with the boxes as soon as I arrive.
gaps.hint: a promise made about the future
gaps.explanation: A promise about the future uses 'will' in the main clause: will help.

gaps.sentence: He rarely ___ his laptop on Sundays because he prefers to rest.
gaps.explanation: Frequency adverbs such as 'rarely' mark habitual actions, which take the present simple: uses.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: This is the best pizza I ___ in years.
gaps.hint: superlative experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Superlative statements about experience up to now take the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.

gaps.sentence: I ___ this temperature to the heat.
gaps.explanation: 'Prefer' is a state verb and takes the present simple: prefer.

gaps.sentence: I ___ exactly what you mean, so there is no need to explain again.
gaps.explanation: 'Understand' is a state verb and is not used in continuous forms, so the present simple is correct.
